title: Apprentice: how a small model learns from a big one

scenes.narration: Your app sends every question to a big AI model. Most are easy. You pay big-model prices anyway.
scenes.visual: Paper background, no title. LEFT (x 10%): the APP, a plain browser-window outline 220x160 px, ink stroke, tiny label 'app'. RIGHT (x 82%): the TEACHER, a tall indigo figure (rounded-rect body, circle head, no face details) behind a wide indigo desk; he is about twice the size of every other character in the film. One ROUTE joins them: a thin ink line with small round dots every 40 px. TOP-RIGHT corner: the COST METER, a small taxi-meter box with an amber frame and rolling ink drum digits starting at '$0.000'. REQUEST CARDS (white index cards 120x80, ink outline, three squiggle lines for the question) are already travelling at frame 0.
beats: 0.0-0.3 s music only; three request cards already sliding app -> teacher; the first one is lettered 'today's sales?'.
on "every question": the stream doubles; a card now leaves the app every 0.4 s.
on "big A I model": camera eases 10% toward the teacher so his size reads against the small cards.
on "Most are easy": as cards pass the midpoint, a tiny green 'easy' tag pops onto 8 of every 10; the other 2 stay untagged.
on "big-model prices": every card, tagged or not, still lands on the teacher's desk; the meter drums spin faster and the single click becomes a rattle.
on "anyway": 6-frame hold on one 'easy' card sitting on the giant desk while the meter keeps rolling.

scenes.narration: What if a small model took the easy ones, and learned the hard ones? That's Apprentice: an open-source gateway that speaks the OpenAI API.
scenes.visual: Same wide layout as the cold open: app left, teacher right, route between, meter top-right. A STUDENT desk is drawn into the middle of the route at x 38%. A dashed 'hosted' line (vertical, light ink dashes) appears at x 70%, separating the teacher from everything else.
beats: on "small model": an ink line draws a small green desk on the route at x 38%; a small green figure (same body shapes as the teacher, half his height) sits down at a laptop.

on "easy ones": the route forks at the desk; every card with a green 'easy' tag peels off to the student, gets green scribbles, and goes back to the app; the meter's rattle slows to occasional clicks.
on "learned the hard ones": an untagged card continues to the teacher; a dotted line traces from the teacher's desk back to the student's desk, and the student turns to watch.
final beat: the app's route detaches from the teacher and snaps to a small port on the box edge labelled 'OpenAI API'

scenes.narration: Change one base URL, and your app never knows.
scenes.visual: A light-theme code editor framed by a simple ink-drawn window on the paper (70% of frame width, centered, thin ink border, no shadow, no gradient).
beats: on "Change one base U R L": the old value 'https://api.openai.com/v1' is selected and replaced by typing 'http://localhost:8000/v1'.
on "never knows": hold; every other line in the file is unchanged.

broll.show: A Python file in a light editor theme with the README's client setup: `from openai import OpenAI` and `client = OpenAI(base_url="http://localhost:8000/v1", api_key="unused")`. Record it as a tiny live edit: cursor selects `https://api.openai.com/v1` inside base_url and types `http://localhost:8000/v1`. Nothing else in the file changes. Font size large enough to read at 1080p.
broll.camera: slow push-in (100% to 112%) centered on the base_url argument, ending tight on 'localhost:8000'.

scenes.narration: First stop, the student: Kwen three, one point seven billion parameters, running on your machine through Ollama. Its answers cost nothing per token.
scenes.visual: Medium shot inside the dashed Apprentice box: the STUDENT desk fills the left 60% of frame. Green figure; laptop with a sticker 'Qwen3 1.7B' and a small 'Ollama' tag on the base. On the desk: a round stopwatch and a little toggle switch labelled 'thinking'. Cost meter small in the top-right corner. Right edge of frame: the dashed 'hosted' line, the teacher soft beyond it.
beats: card lands on the desk
ink underline under the 'Qwen3 1.7B' sticker
'local' outline draws around desk
green lines are written; corner meter stays still
card returns to the app
scenes.transition: continuous pan right along the route to the judge booth (no cut)

scenes.narration: Small models slip up, so a judge checks every answer. Meet Kev, a tiny open model.
scenes.visual: The pan lands on the JUDGE BOOTH at x 55% inside the Apprentice box: an amber podium with a small figure holding a magnifying glass. On the booth front, a semicircular DIAL GAUGE from 0 to 1 with a single notch at 0.8. A rubber stamp rests on the ledge.
beats: on "Small models slip up": quick cut-in on the student's card: one of the green lines bends off course as it is written (the viewer sees it, the student does not).
on "a judge checks every answer": the card slides to the booth; the amber magnifier sweeps across each line, left to right; the bent line darkens under the lens.
on "Kev": a nameplate drops onto the booth with a small bounce: 'Kev 0.8B'.
on "tiny open model": the gauge needle twitches but does not settle (it pays off two scenes later).

scenes.narration: Fine-tuning on Colab took Kev from forty-six to ninety-nine percent accuracy.
scenes.visual: Ink-drawn browser frame on the paper, 72% of frame width, left-aligned. The right 25% of the frame is bare paper reserved for one hand-lettered amber annotation.
beats: on "fine-tuned on Colab": the window settles; the training progress bar is moving.
on "under half right": in the paper margin, amber ink letters '45.7%'.
on "ninety-nine percent": an amber arrow draws from it to '99.3%', with a tiny 'held-out' label underneath.

broll.show: Google Colab in light theme with notebook train_sql_judge.ipynb open (file name readable in the tab/title). The fine-tuning cell is running: its progress bar advances and loss lines print under it. Do not edit or fake numbers inside the screen capture; the 45.7% -> 99.3% figures live only in the paper-margin annotation.
broll.camera: slow push-in on the progress bar and the log output below it.

scenes.transition: cut back to the judge booth

scenes.narration: Kev scores its confidence. Zero point eight or higher, the answer goes straight back.
scenes.visual: Judge booth center frame; the dial gauge is large (about 30% of frame height). From the booth the route runs two ways: left back to the app, and right across the dashed 'hosted' line to the teacher.
beats: on "scores its confidence": a fresh student card with all green lines straight sits under the magnifier; the needle swings and settles at 0.93; '0.93' prints on a small amber tab under the gauge.
on "Zero point eight": the 0.8 notch flashes amber twice.
on "or higher": the stamp lifts and thunks down: a green 'APPROVED' mark on the card, with a small paper shake.
on "straight back": the card zips left along the route to the app; the route segment it travels is re-inked green behind it.

scenes.narration: Lower, and it escalates to the teacher: G L M five point two, a big open-weight model.
scenes.visual: Same booth framing, then the camera follows the card right across the 'hosted' line to the indigo TEACHER desk (same tall figure as the cold open). Cost meter visible top-right throughout.
beats: on "Lower": the card with the bent line goes under the glass; the needle settles at 0.41, left of the notch; the tab reads '0.41'; the stamp thunks a red 'REJECTED' mark.
on "escalates to the teacher": the card slides right; the dashed 'hosted' line lifts like a gate as it crosses; camera follows to the teacher.
on "G L M five point two": nameplate 'GLM-5.2' drops onto the desk with a small 'open weights' tag; the teacher writes clean indigo lines on a new card.
as the teacher finishes: the cost meter clicks exactly once, visibly (one drum step).
on "open-weight model": the indigo card heads back left toward the Apprentice box.
scenes.transition: continuous pan left following the indigo card back into the Apprentice box

scenes.narration: The trick: every teacher answer goes into memory.
scenes.visual: Inside the Apprentice box, below the student desk, the previously empty slot fills: the MEMORY, an orange two-drawer filing cabinet, label 'memory', small side label 'SQLite + nomic-embed-text'.
beats: on "The trick": the indigo card coming back from the teacher stops above the cabinet; a carbon copy peels off it (offset 6 px, then separates).
on "every teacher answer": a small orange stamp prints a row of 6 dots of different sizes along the copy's top edge: its fingerprint.
on "into memory": the top drawer slides open, the copy drops in with its tab sticking up, the drawer closes with a small bump; the original card continues to the app.

scenes.narration: When a similar question arrives, the student gets that worked example and usually solves it alone.
scenes.visual: Wide view of the whole Apprentice box: student desk, judge booth, memory cabinet; teacher beyond the 'hosted' line at right; cost meter top-right.
beats: on "similar question": a new request card arrives; its squiggles differ but the orange stamp gives it the same 6-dot fingerprint; the matching tab in the cabinet lifts and thin orange lines join dot to dot between the two.
on "worked example": the drawer opens and the indigo-inked card floats up and pins beside the student's laptop.
on "solves it alone": the student writes green lines following the pinned card; the card goes to the judge; needle settles at 0.91; green APPROVED; card returns to the app.
throughout: the teacher leans back idle and the cost meter does not move.

scenes.narration: So the student takes more traffic over time, and the bill shrinks.
scenes.visual: Full-system wide shot, every element smaller: app left, Apprentice box center (student, judge, memory), teacher beyond the 'hosted' line right, cost meter top-right. Under the box, a thin horizontal bar labelled 'student' with a green fill.
beats: on "So": time-lapse at 4x: cards stream through the system continuously.
the memory cabinet fills: tabs pile up; when two drawers are full a third drawer draws itself in.
on "takes more traffic": more and more cards turn back at the student desk; the green 'student' bar slides from about a quarter of its width to most of it; trips across the 'hosted' line become rare.
on "the bill shrinks": the cost meter's drum rolls slower and slower until it barely clicks.
scenes.transition: cut to the dashboard B-roll frame

scenes.narration: We tested it on eighty held-out text-to-S Q L questions.
scenes.visual: A stack of 80 small question cards on the left feeds into the full stage; a tally board above the stage counts answered questions.
beats: cards fan out from the stack into a 10x8 grid of small squares
on 'held-out': a dashed line separates them from the memory cabinet (never seen in training)

scenes.narration: New student: twenty-five percent. Teacher: one hundred. Apprentice, after learning: ninety-seven and a half.
scenes.visual: Paper background, three horizontal lanes stacked. Each lane: a short label at left, then a grid of 80 small rounded squares (10 columns x 8 rows, 14 px, ink outlines), one square per held-out question, and a rolling percentage at the right end. Small label '80 questions' above the top grid.
beats: lane 1: 20 green, 60 red outline -> 25%
lane 2: 80 indigo -> 100%
lane 3: 67 green, 11 indigo, 2 red outline -> 97.5% (78/80 correct)
scenes.transition: lanes 1 and 2 slide away; lane 3 moves to center (continuous)

scenes.narration: The student handled eighty-six percent of requests, and the bill was eighty-seven percent smaller than teacher-only.
scenes.visual: The Apprentice grid centered in the top half. Below it, two copies of the cost meter from the cold open, side by side: left labelled 'teacher only', right labelled 'Apprentice'.
beats: green (67) + red (2) squares = 69 handled by the student slide into one block: 86%; 11 indigo into a smaller block
on "the bill": both meters start rolling at the same speed; the right meter clicks only while an indigo square lights up.
on "eighty-seven percent smaller": left meter stops at '$0.126', right meter at '$0.0165'; a bracket draws between them with '-87%'.

scenes.narration: The catch: on question shapes it has never seen, Apprentice gets fifty-three percent, the student alone thirty-three. Memory works best on repeats.
scenes.visual: Back inside the Apprentice box, medium shot on the student desk and the memory cabinet; two short horizontal bars will draw on the right third of the frame.
beats: on "The catch": a request card with a different silhouette arrives (clipped corners, almost hexagonal) and gets an unfamiliar dot fingerprint.
on "never seen": the drawer opens; orange lines try to join its dots to each tab and none line up; the drawer closes with nothing; the student tilts his head once.
on "fifty-three percent": bar 'Apprentice 53%' draws at right (ink outline, green and indigo fill).
on "thirty-three": bar 'student alone 33%' draws beneath it, green, shorter.
on "works best on repeats": a familiar rectangular card arrives; its dots snap to a tab instantly; the worked example pins up; quick green APPROVED.
scenes.transition: cut to the Kirana B-roll frame

scenes.narration: Real questions repeat. A shop owner asks, in Hinglish, which store had the most orders. The student answers alone, for free.
scenes.visual: Stage; the app is a shop counter chat. A card lettered 'March 2026 mein sabse zyada orders kis store pe aaye?' goes to the student; answer card 'Bandra Linking Road · 65 orders'; judge 0.96 APPROVED; meter stays $0.0000.
beats: question card travels to the student
student writes; memory tab lifts (remembered 3)
judge needle 0.96, APPROVED
answer returns: 'Bandra Linking Road · 65 orders'

scenes.narration: A support bot answering refund questions. When the student answers, your data never leaves your machine.
scenes.visual: Full-system wide shot again (same layout as the flywheel). The app slot at the left is redrawn in ink for each use case.
beats: on "support bot": the app slot redraws as a chat window labelled 'QuickBite'; three cards tagged 'refund?' flow in: the first goes to the teacher and drops a copy into memory, the next two are answered by the student and approved.
on "coding agent": the slot redraws as a small terminal labelled 'agent'; a quick burst of about 20 tiny cards; nearly all turn at the student desk; the meter barely clicks.

on "your data stays local": a thin dashed outline labelled 'your machine' draws around the app slot and the whole Apprentice box; green cards circulate inside it while the route to the teacher fades to a faint dotted line.

scenes.narration: Apprentice. Open source, open models, M I T licensed.
scenes.visual: The complete system from the whole film, then simplified: app, Apprentice box (student, judge, memory), teacher beyond the 'hosted' line, meter. It tidies into one compact row of small outlined icons with the name and repo URL lettered beneath.
beats: on 'Apprentice': the whole stage scales to 55% and moves up; one last card runs the loop and gets APPROVED
on "Open source, open models": under the row, ink lettering 'Apprentice', and beneath it 'github.com/Ayush-e4/apprentice'.
on "M I T licensed": a small 'MIT' tag is lettered to the right of the URL.
final 2.5 s, music only: hold on the diagram and URL; the corner meter stays still; fade to plain paper.
